media:group.media:title: Humanity's Greatest Engineering Feat?
media:group.media:description:
Adam Savage visits Smithsonian's @airandspace for a first look at an extraordinary new addition to the collection: the Pathfinder for the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)! Space history curator Samantha Thompson walks Adam through this full-scale engineering model, which was essential to proving out the telescope's multi-stage origami unfolding, extreme temperature tolerances, and precision optics before the real JWST launched a million miles into deep space. Adam inspects the massive backplane structure, the secondary mirror assembly, and two real beryllium hexagonal mirrors — one uncoated and one coated in microscopically thin gold — to explore the engineering marvels that paved the way for one of humanity's greatest engineering achievements!

entry.title: Uncovering the Secrets of a Rare WWI Fabric Biplane

media:group.media:title: Uncovering the Secrets of a Rare WWI Fabric Biplane
media:group.media:description:
It's been five years since Adam Savage first saw this Lincoln-Standard Tourabout (Modified Standard J-1) at @airandspace's Mary Baker Engen Restoration Hangar, and it's time to check in on the aircraft's progress courtesy of museum specialists Jay Flanagan and Heather Moosher! From uncovering improvised barnstormer repairs (like fruit-crate wood hidden inside the wings) and matching period-accurate lumber to the art of envelope-sewing, rib stitching, and applying butyrate dope to cotton fabric, see how the Smithsonian team honors early aviation craftspeople while preserving this iconic biplane for future generations.
